content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks with no errors, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 636 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of your own code in the bundle.

I did not run a side-by-side comparison against the original, so criterion (1) is untested. Reading the es-toolkit source, the behaviour should be identical for the input ranges you gave. `src/module.ts` can't be built or type-checked here because `node_modules` has no lodash, so I couldn't measure its size either. That means I can't confirm the 95 bytes of own code is within the allowance over the original.

| lodash | es-toolkit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `mapValues` | `mapValues` from `es-toolkit` | Same behaviour for plain objects. |
| `keyBy(rows, 'name')` | `keyBy(rows, (row) => row.name)` | The strict `keyBy` doesn't accept the string shorthand, so I added a small callback. |
| `isEmpty` | `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat` | Strict `es-toolkit` has no `isEmpty`, and only compat does. |

I kept the compat `isEmpty` because it preserves the lodash behaviour: `null`, booleans and integers count as empty, strings and collections are empty only when they have no length or keys. I didn't use lodash here since it isn't installed and compat covers the case.

The exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged.
